result.summary:
R7b is built. There is a new builder `scripts/race3d/builders/landmarks.gd` with its own shader `assets/shaders/modern/landmark.gdshader`. Every landmark Arcade shows now stands at Arcade's anchor on the path, out to 1,900 m. It uses Arcade's law (`RoadRenderer.landmark_fade`, unit test deviation < 1e-5) and the night floodlight. Beyond 0.70 L it fades with a translucent variant instead of the dither (B-09); at full coverage that variant is pixel-identical to the opaque one (measured 0 of 921,600 px).

Representation follows one order, which is the AS6 interface: a manifest model first, then Arcade's picture, then Arcade's procedural kind built as a real 3D shape (domed church, TV tower, lighthouse with beams, skyscraper group; N2), then the fallback set. No instance uniforms (A-19).

`layers/backdrop.gd` now draws the destination skyline as Arcade does: sprite silhouettes, plus Arcade's own 2D drawings through a RoadRenderer that is never added to the tree. A silhouette fades out while its 3D landmark is in range. `props.gd` needed no change: the skip for landmarks was already there (lines 88, 122, 329, 539, 741).

All gates were run on 2c154bc: import, scripts 334/0, one full run_tests (passed), golden 20/20 and 17/17, render checks 29/29, sight and path --full, and whole Modern stages without script errors next to base. Modern golden is 5/6: `modern_s4_mittel` changes on purpose by at most 2/255 at the Michel. It was not regenerated, because A-18 leaves that to the integration.

Pictures: the procedural shapes look better than Arcade by day. Weaker than Arcade: the aviation light is about 3× Arcade's dot, and from 260 m in bends the domed shapes sit up to about 85 px off Arcade's drawing.

result.look_verdict:
Measured on llvmpipe, pictures at Hoch.

Better than Arcade: the procedural landmarks are real 3D shapes. By day they read better than Arcade's flat drawings and much better than the old wide fallback card: the Belgrade church with green domes, the slim Dortmund TV tower with its basket, the Madrid glass towers with floor bands, and the Hannover town hall dome.

Equal to Arcade: pictures (Elbphilharmonie, Kaiserburg, Eiffel tower, Atomium, Koekelberg) sit at Arcade's place and look the same. At night they are floodlit or lit like Arcade, and the Hamburg and Paris clips show no jump or dither. The skyline sits on the panorama like Arcade's, with no doubling. Below the horizon the far ground reads as land at S1-S5 and the arrivals.

Worse than Arcade: the red aviation light of the TV tower is about 3x Arcade's dot, and the tower shaft is brighter at night. The Elbphilharmonie is a little brighter at night. In bends at about 260 m the domed shapes sit up to about 85 px (6-7 %) off Arcade's flat drawing: Leipzig is lower and further left, Belgrade wider and further right, because the shape turns with the road and the dome stands 25 m behind its front. The lighthouse beams were hardly visible in the one frame taken.

Missing: real landmark models (AS6). The 600-m arrival views mostly do not show the landmark at all, because houses hide it in both modes, so near views were added.

result.summary:
The bend sight corridor is now built from the real road geometry (A-17). It is the envelope of all sight lines of length L along the actual path, with the camera on every row in every lane; L = min(300 m, F2 need/0.6 + 9 m). The code is scripts/race3d/sight_corridor.gd, computed once per stage and precomputed by the streamer. Terrain, props, city fences and border pillars all read this one envelope. F7 checks it against an independent reference: 0 of 388,907 cross-section sides left uncovered across the whole network (measured).

What comes back (measured, 128 directions): 23,026 props (16,947 trees, 1,878 city houses) and none newly dropped. City fences: 75.3 % of Arcade's (was 64.3 %). The Belgrad–Sofia border roof stands on four pillars again. In the pictures the compositions now match Arcade: the T2 tree group, the start oak, the house rows in München, Belgrad and Hannover.

F2 holds: modern_sight --full 0.593/0.596/0.555, and the occlusion probe stays visible up to L at T1–T4, S0 and S4. At C1, 270 m was already hidden in the base.

Two problems found during the work:
(1) The props builder (R7c) tests only an object's foot point. 5,832 props reach into the envelope with their near edge or crown (base: 1,124). The reach-aware test is built in ChunkContext.in_bend_corridor(); R7c still has to call it.
(2) The perf run showed main-thread spikes of up to 24 ms. 7d8bbb6 now precomputes the corridor past landmark_path_m. At timescale 4: equal to base, no recomputation after loading.

Gates: Arcade goldens 20/20 and 17/17; Modern 2/6 (changes intended and viewed, no modern-make); 28 render checks green; sight and path --full green; unit tests 811 with 2–3 audio failures that also fail on the base under the same load.

A-18 '5 of 48 roofs': on this base 4 of the 48 race-stage roofs hang (measured), plus the dev_testetappe roof (picture R5), which makes 5 but not 'of 48'. Now 3 plus the test stage.
A-18 (packages don't regenerate modern_slice.*) vs the brief ('modern-make where changed on purpose'): followed A-18.
'Camera in every lane' was built with lane centres, like modern_sight F1-lanes. A car on the shoulder is not covered.

A-17 (2) 'nothing >0.5 m in the envelope' needs footprints, but the corridor interface was a point test, and the builder that calls it belongs to another package (R7c). Measured 5,832 props reach in (base 1,124, up to 19 m deep). Suggestion: make reach/half_len mandatory for builders that place objects wider than 1 m near bends.
notes_for_next: R7c (props.gd): in drop_reason() and the cover test, call ctx.in_bend_corridor(z, x, reach, half_len). reach = |anchor x| - |near edge x| (align: edge: extent x scale; otherwise crown radius = width x scale / 2); half_len = width x scale / 2. Measured effect: 269 left (all non-droppable), 15,954 back instead of 22,432, 1,223 base-drawn props dropped. This fixes C1 at 270 m.
R7c: merge the test_props.gd hunk (fixture now chunk 13, rows 418+i*3) with your own changes.
station.gd bend_corridor_at() could read the exact envelope (tp.sight.width_near(k, side)) like border.gd instead of the rounded encoding.

result.look_verdict:
Better than the base wherever bends had emptied the scenery. T2: the whole left tree group is back and now matches Arcade with shaded models, better than Arcade. S0: the start oak is back. München: the pink house row on the left is back; the base showed an empty square. Belgrad: the right house row and the poplar are back; the base showed a bare meadow. Hannover: the big corner house is back. T1: two firs back; T4: a rock and fir group back; T3: the far rocks back. R1: the roof stands on pillars like Arcade.

Unchanged: C1, where Arcade's park tree is still missing (L=300 m in cities), and the near rocks on the inside of T3/T4. These stand in the sight lines, so this is correct by the rule but differs from Arcade. Bern, Nürnberg and Lyon frames are unchanged.

Still worse than Arcade: R2-R5 roofs hang from masts with stays, because the pillar would stand 3.6-12.8 m inside the sight lines. In the clip, two near outside firs in the S-bends are missing.

Risk: some returned houses and crowns overhang into the envelope (the foot-point issue). At C1 this removed the last 9 px of the car at 270 m, though that spot was already hidden in the base. Medium shows the same compositions as high. Popping cannot be judged from stills.

result.verdict: R7b is solid. Nothing in it is broken, and it can go into RINT-M3 after two small night-look fixes (B-01, B-02). I measured every gate myself on 2c154bc. Arcade golden check: 20/20 and 17/17 identical. A full run_tests passed (945 s). modern_sight and modern_path_check --full both passed. 6 of 6 selected render checks passed, and the stage result matches the base. A data scan of all 143 landmarks in 128 stage directions found no difference from Arcade in representation, set, scale or tint, and every landmark builds headless. The new tests guard their rules: 16 of 18 mutations were caught. The two that slipped through are the floodlight on plain props (B-03). File ownership was kept, apart from one foreign test file that R7b reported itself. The look was judged against Arcade and the base on the same simulation state. By day, the 3D shapes are clearly better than the base, which drew wide stand-in blocks at Dortmund, Madrid, Calais, Hannover and Belgrade. Hannover and Dortmund also look better than Arcade's flat drawings. Sprite landmarks look the same as Arcade. Worse than Arcade: at night the Elbphilharmonie is about 28 % brighter than both Arcade and the base. The aviation light is about 23 times Arcade's dot area, not the 3 times the R7b report claims. Close up, the domed shapes sit lower or to the side: Leipzig's dome is hidden behind a tree, and Belgrade's is about 85 px off. The unmirrored church on the left side stands up to 37.8 m closer to the road than in Arcade. At most 600-m city arrivals, houses hide the landmark in all three modes, so those views cannot show a difference.

findings.where: assets/shaders/modern/landmark.gdshader CE_PICTURE, `vec3 col = mix(x, lit, wl)` (~l.236)
findings.problem: Sprite landmarks at night are brighter than Arcade and than the base. The picture and its light layer are blended in linear space, while Arcade and billboard.gdshader (l.168) blend in display space. This affects all 32 sprite landmarks that have a light layer, including the Elbphilharmonie on the test-build stage.
findings.evidence: Measured: deliver/QA-R7b/raw/hamburg_22_{arcade,basis,modern}_00.png, facade box (300..380, 232..268). Mean luminance Arcade 112.7, base 116.2, R7b 144.5; p90 178/178/197. Zoom: deliver/QA-R7b/bilder/elbphilharmonie_nacht_zoom.png
findings.fix: Blend in display space like billboard.gdshader: disp = mix(min(d,1), min(l.rgb,1), wl); col = srgb_to_lin(disp) + to_lin(base)*headlight_color*v_head*(1-wl). Add a render check that the Elbphilharmonie facade at 22:00 stays at most 1.1x Arcade.

findings.where: scripts/race3d/builders/landmarks.gd _tv_tower/_skyscrapers kit.glow(0.6, 5.0/3.0 m, 2.5 px); landmark.gdshader CE_GLOW
findings.problem: The red aviation light of the 3D TV tower and the skyscrapers is much larger than Arcade's dot: about 4.5x the diameter and 23x the area. The post glow pass inflates it further. The R7b report says 'about 3x'. The flugfeuer check only caps it at 3 % of the frame.
findings.evidence: Measured: raw/dortmund_22_*, red pixels (r>=110, r>1.8g, r>1.8b): Arcade 10 (4x4 px), R7b 232 (17x19 px). Same on the Deck preset (238 vs about 16). Madrid at 22:00 is similar. Zoom: bilder/dortmund_nacht_flugfeuer_zoom.png
findings.repro: abc.sh <out> high 1280x720 --stage=bremen_dortmund --from=bremen --start-km=225.0 --hour=22 (other arguments as in B-01)
findings.fix: Use Arcade's size (_lm_glow: radius max(2.5 px, 6 m*s), core 0.35 r), e.g. size 1.5 m, minimum 1.5 px, strength <=0.35 so the glow pass does not bloom it. Bound flugfeuer to at most 3x Arcade's red pixels at the same spot.

findings.where: landmarks.gd _domed_church (body to -44 m, main dome at z=-22*k) and _place (turned with the road at the anchor)
findings.problem: Domed shapes stand with their front face at the anchor, while Arcade draws the dome at the anchor. Close up, the dome therefore sits lower and smaller, and in bends the shape shows its side wall.
findings.evidence: Measured in pictures: raw/nah_leipzig_12_* – Arcade's dome is visible above a tree, but hidden in Modern (bilder/leipzig_nah_kuppel_verdeckt.png). raw/nah_belgrad_12_* – about 85 px right of Arcade and wider. Hannover matches Arcade.
findings.fix: Move shapes forward by half their depth (main dome at the anchor). Orient each one once, towards the bearing from the path point about 600 m before it, instead of the road heading at the anchor (see contract issue V-1).

findings.problem: Arcade mirrors props/church on the left side (mirror_left); Modern never mirrors. As a result the tower stands up to 37.8 m closer to the road. That is 44.7 px at 600 m, inside the 64 px limit, but the report gives 24.7 px as the maximum.
findings.evidence: Measured: data scan m1/QA-R7b/scan_landmarks.log, largest offset Magdeburger Dom leipzig_magdeburg__leipzig, Arcade x -90.38 vs Modern -52.62. raw/flood2_bremen_22_*: tower about 63 px right of Arcade's at about 380 m (bilder/bremer_dom_nacht_380m_zoom.png)
findings.fix: Lead decision under D24: either place the model at Arcade's mirrored anchor (edge_anchor_x(x, side, true, ext, sc); the body moves away from the road), or mirror the single MeshInstance3D with negative x scale.

findings.where: landmark.gdshader CE_ATLAS `alb = mix(alb, alb*flood_color*1.6, flood)`; tests
findings.problem: The floodlight on plain props used as landmarks (43 of 143) only scales the lit albedo, so at night it adds little. No test notices if it is removed.
findings.evidence: Measured: raw/flood2_bremen_22_*, tower box mean RGB Arcade 102/106/73, base 79/101/62, R7b 89/106/63. Mutations M16 and M17 (floodlight removed in CE_ATLAS / CE_PICTURE) were NOT caught by test_landmarks or check_landmarks (m1/QA-R7b/mutlogs/mutate_flood.log)
findings.fix: Add EMISSION += alb*flood_color*flood*k in CE_ATLAS (as channel 14 does). Add a check, e.g. a render check that the Bremer Dom tower at 22:00 reaches at least 0.85x Arcade.

findings.where: scripts/race3d/layers/backdrop.gd (_sky_sig rounds alpha to 0.015, so the whole canvas is redrawn on every fade step)
findings.problem: Redrawing the skyline causes main-thread spikes.
findings.evidence: Measured under load 8-10: backdrop hook max 3.0 / 4.3 ms on whole Deck stages, against 0.56 / 1.43 ms on the base; the averages differ by only +0.02-0.04 ms (gates/perf_*_deck_12.log)
findings.repro: m1/QA-R7b/sh/perf.sh (run_stage deck kiel_hamburg / bremen_dortmund, head vs base)
findings.fix: Round alpha more coarsely (0.05), or during fades redraw at most every second frame.

findings.problem: Latent cache collision: the key uses height_m*scale, but the mesh is built from height_m and the node carries the scale. Two entries of the same kind and colours with an equal product but different scale would get a wrongly sized mesh. The proc_mesh comment ('node carries no scale') is also wrong.
findings.evidence: Code read. The data scan finds no such pair in the network today (inferred: latent only).
findings.fix: Key on height_m alone and correct the comment.

findings.problem: Two statements are wrong. 'Heute: nur landmarks/michel' as a model: in fact 46 of 143 landmarks draw as models (props/church 38, props/building_tall 5, michel 3). '24.7 px' is given as the maximum offset; network-wide it is 44.7 px.
